proposed_from.topic: Population identification of innovation-atomic causal units in grouped additive-noise models. For observed scalar coordinates with a smooth positive density, define admissible partitions by C3 additive block mechanisms, mutually independent smooth positive block noises, causal minimality, Göbler edgewise Condition-1 restrictions, and innovation atomicity: no nontrivial coordinate split of a block noise admits an additive-noise representation in either direction. Prove that every admissible law has one refinement-minimal coordinate partition equal to the generating causal units and one labelled block DAG, excluding all incomparable crossings; give assumption-removal converses and a finite-dimensional certification corollary. Distinguish Niu and Rajpal joint-learning algorithms and audit the Bosch 19-process grouping. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: For two empty-DAG representations, smooth log-density decompositions over both partitions force decomposition over common-refinement cells, so every crossed block innovation splits independently and violates atomicity. For the three-coordinate crossing {1,2}<-{3} versus {1,3}<-{2}, equating conditional densities yields an exact translation-family equation; on every nonsingular chart it forces alternative conditional innovation laws to be translates, while the identically singular case conflicts with nondegenerate independent noise. The disclosed quadratic/Gaussian four-variable threat is inadmissible because both middle-block innovations are explicit scalar ANMs. Searches found joint grouping algorithms and interventional/temporal partition results, but no population uniqueness theorem. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Globalize the local translation-family conclusion, or prove an equivalent nondescendant-conditioning lemma, for arbitrary crossing blocks when conditioning selects coordinates from a correlated alternative innovation. EARLY KILL TEST: Complete the smooth-positive three-coordinate crossing lemma first; one solution with both bivariate innovations atomic and every edgewise Condition-1 clause satisfied should immediately stop the kernel.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: Atomic unknown-partition recovery is the sole new identification kernel, and it requires both incomparable-crossing rigidity and strict-refinement rigidity. Observable density regularity is derived rather than assumed. Innovation atomicity is stated with exact quantifiers over \(C^3\) maps and residual laws in \(\operatorname{SmoothPos}(m)\), whose full positivity already supplies nondegeneracy. A splitwise conditional characteristic-function modulus criterion is an observable sufficient condition rather than a restatement of that existential exclusion; conditional covariance variation is only a sufficient directional diagnostic. GoblerWindischDrton2025 identifies a graph after a vector partition is supplied, and its exact Condition 1 Equation (3) and Corollary 1 are preserved without extra rank restrictions. PetersEtAl2014 identifies a restricted ANM DAG on scalar vertices. The strict non-scalar frontier is witnessed for every \(\theta=(a,b,c_0,d_0,\lambda)\in(0,\infty)^5\): normalization and positive log-\(C^3\) density follow directly, dependence follows from the nonzero mixed log-density derivative, and both directional ANMs are excluded because the relevant conditional variance is strictly decreasing in \(d_0+\lambda u^2\) or \(c_0+\lambda v^2\). This is an open parameter family within one exponential-polynomial model, not a genericity theorem. EntnerHoyer2012 assumes known groups and estimates a causal order in a linear non-Gaussian model. None of the comparators controls crossed partitions or extracts a forbidden coarse-noise split from a strict refinement.

seed_details.kernel: Prove that innovation atomicity plus fixed-partition GANM asymmetry makes \(P\mapsto(\pi^\star,G^\star)\) single-valued over all coordinate partitions.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the fixed common vertex set in the Peters--Göbler sink-disagreement reduction by the overlap cells of two competing partitions.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for unknown-partition grouped ANM identification found CIC, variational cluster-DAG learning, fixed-group theory, and linear independent-subspace uniqueness, but no theorem excluding crossed atomic partitions.
seed_details.opened_evidence: The anchor's Introduction treats groups as the causal quantities; Definition 2 and Corollary 1 fix the groups before identifying the DAG; Appendix A conditions on common group vertices; the Conclusion lists smoothness and confounding limitations but does not identify the partition.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is immediate from GoblerWindischDrton2025 because Condition 1 already identifies a vector GANM. Rebuttal: that corollary quantifies over DAGs on one supplied partition, and its conditioning set is not valid when it cuts through a correlated innovation of another partition.

seed_details.kernel: Classify every positive \(C^3\) law admitting the crossings \(\{1,2\}|\{3\}\) and \(\{1,3\}|\{2\}\), with atomicity failure or an explicit reversible exception as the exhaustive alternatives.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Differentiate an equality between two overlapping vector-innovation factorizations rather than two scalar forward and backward factorizations.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches located scalar ANM and post-nonlinear reversible-family classifications and the vector Condition 1 paper, but no overlap-conditioned three-coordinate classification.
seed_details.opened_evidence: The anchor's Introduction motivates asymmetry from nonlinear additive noise; Theorem 1 derives Equation 4 from the mixed-to-pure second-derivative ratio; Appendix A solves the resulting first-order equation for the second derivative of the input log-density; the Conclusion claims only generic scalar identification.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is Hoyer's differential equation with vector notation. Rebuttal: the shared coordinate belongs to different innovations in the two models, so conditioning changes the innovation law and the scalar ratio argument does not globalize automatically.

seed_details.kernel: Give an assumption-indexed necessity atlas for positivity, minimality, atomicity, and each tensor Condition 1 clause while preserving all untouched conditions.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace scalar reversible-edge examples by same-law pairs whose two representations are both minimal under their own coordinate partitions.
seed_details.destination_search: Park2020 supplies a variance-based alternative to differential asymmetry, while ZhangHyvarinen2009 classifies scalar reversible families; no unknown-partition necessity atlas was found.
seed_details.opened_evidence: Peters et al. Definition 27 imposes conditional bivariate restrictions, Theorem 28 proves DAG identification, Proposition 29 supplies the graph disagreement, and the Discussion separates identification from algorithmic scalability.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: the atlas is a list of textbook failures. Rebuttal: atomicity and directional-asymmetry removals admit legal witnesses, but the scan shows that isolated minimality and smoothness removals interact with Condition 1 and do not yet yield a clean complete atlas.
seed_details.drop_reason: A full iff atlas would require disentangling causal minimality from an edgewise nonidentity condition that may already exclude null mechanisms; only the two clean converses are retained in the selected proposal.

seed_details.kernel: Characterize the unique finest coordinate partition of a positive density into mutually independent innovation-atomic blocks by the meet of every independent partition.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace linear unmixing equivalence by density intersection over two coordinate partitions.
seed_details.destination_search: The 2012 independent-subspace theorem identifies unknown irreducible subspace dimensions under linear mixing, but no causal or coordinate-partition version was located.
seed_details.opened_evidence: The publisher abstract states finite-covariance uniqueness up to trivial indeterminacies and identifies subspace dimensions; the accessible predecessor defines irreducibility and builds uniqueness from decompositions into irreducible components.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is just the intersection property of conditional independence. Rebuttal: the objection holds for the empty-DAG case, so the result is retained only as a base lemma rather than the paper's kernel.

seed_details.kernel: On a degree-bounded exponential-polynomial GANM class, reduce admissibility and uniqueness to a finite coefficient and real-quantifier-elimination certificate.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Upgrade SCORE's fixed-scalar score-Jacobian zero pattern to a complete bounded-degree search over partitions, graphs, mechanisms, and internal innovation splits.
seed_details.destination_search: Derivative criteria and characteristic-kernel independence tests were found, but no finite sound-and-complete certificate for unknown atomic GANM groups.
seed_details.opened_evidence: The anchor's Introduction identifies the score Jacobian as a scalable population object; its main recovery argument uses leafwise score-variance structure; the Conclusion does not address unknown grouping or certificate completeness.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: finite dimension makes certification automatic. Rebuttal: full atomicity quantifies over arbitrary smooth internal ANMs, so a separate polynomial split-completeness theorem is indispensable and is exposed as an open question.

seed_details.kernel: Characterize when the population CIC maximizer and the zero-temperature variational ELBO target the same cluster DAG, and derive a smooth positive GANM regime where they diverge.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Normalize CIC's sample-size-dependent MDL score and Rajpal's prior-sensitive ELBO to comparable population objectives.
seed_details.destination_search: The Niu paper and Rajpal preprint compare empirically, but neither gives a common population target or an equivalence frontier.
seed_details.opened_evidence: Niu's Introduction frames synergy and faithfulness; Equation 6 defines CIC from total correlation, mutual information, and MDL; Algorithms 1--2 use random initialization and greedy moves; the Conclusion claims a tractable first step, not consistency. Rajpal's Propositions 1--2 are ELBO identities and its Conclusion is empirical.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: both are generic model-selection scores and will agree under correct specification. Rebuttal: CIC rewards synergy and uses a combinatorial description penalty, whereas the ELBO depends on likelihood, priors, and a restricted variational family; equality is not automatic.

seed_details.kernel: Build a multiplicity-aware ledger of within-process refinements and selected crossings for the 19 supplied Bosch process groups, separating real-data evidence from semisynthetic population facts.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace validation against a supplied partial order by explicit residual-ANM tests for refinements and crossings of the supplied grouping.
seed_details.destination_search: The causalAssembly paper supplies partial physical knowledge and a Markov semisynthetic generator; no published atomicity audit of the 19 process blocks was located.
seed_details.opened_evidence: The causalAssembly Introduction emphasizes missing real causal ground truth; its construction fits conditional distributions under a partially physics-informed graph; the grouped GANM application uses 19 supplied groups comprising 121 features and samples 5000 of roughly 35000 parts.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is a dataset reanalysis without a theorem. Rebuttal: the objection holds unless coupled to a sound certificate, so the audit is retained only as the finite-certificate consumer and not as the kernel.

seed_details.kernel: Replace tensor Condition 1 by a block conditional-variance ordering and prove unknown atomic-partition plus DAG identification under that alternative restriction.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Extend Park's scalar source-order comparison to vector blocks while cluster membership is unknown.
seed_details.destination_search: Park proves scalar DAG recovery under conditional-variance restrictions, while the grouped GANM paper uses a differential nonidentity; no unknown-block variance theorem was found.
seed_details.opened_evidence: Park's Introduction motivates unequal error variances; the main identifiability condition orders conditional variances without restricting functional form; the algorithm recursively recovers sources; the Conclusion does not treat vector groups or latent partitions.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is a routine scalar-to-vector extension. Rebuttal: unknown partitions make conditioning and variance comparison non-invariant under crossings, but the required block ordering appears at least as difficult as the selected crossing lemma and offers less direct evidence.
